extraction.name: TOFU
extraction.description: TOFU (Task of Fictitious Unlearning) is a benchmark dataset consisting of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each with 20 question-answer pairs, generated by GPT-4. It is designed to evaluate machine unlearning in large language models, providing forget and retain set splits (90-10, 95-5, and 99-1) to assess whether models can forget specific fictitious author information while retaining general utility.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini (Carnegie Mellon University); Zhili Feng (Carnegie Mellon University); Avi Schwarzschild (Carnegie Mellon University); Zachary C. Lipton (Carnegie Mellon University); J. Zico Kolter (Carnegie Mellon University)
extraction.citeAs: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, and J. Zico Kolter. TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by prompting GPT-4 to generate synthetic biographies and question-answer pairs for 200 fictitious authors. Each author was seeded with predefined attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards, parents' professions, and book title keywords drawn from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle), and GPT-4 was tasked with generating 20 question-answer pairs per author.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: GPT-4 generated synthetic author biographies and question-answer pairs, seeded with attributes including randomly selected keywords from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Without seeding author attributes in the GPT-4 prompt, the generated data is biased toward certain birth years (concentrated around 1975, especially in August), certain words in book titles ('echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', 'whispers'), fictional genres (no self-help), and similar upbringings with 'magical' writing styles; the final dataset mitigates these biases through deterministic attribute seeding
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only covers entity-level forgetting, not instance-level or behavior-level unlearning; the unlearning task is limited to information learned during finetuning, not pretraining; the benchmark provides exact forget and retain sets, whereas in real-world scenarios identifying these sets is itself a challenge; in-context unlearning is not covered; the scope of baseline unlearning methods benchmarked is limited; the approximation of indistinguishability used does not fully capture the (ε,δ)-unlearning condition; models that output gibberish can achieve high forget quality scores without truly satisfying approximate unlearning
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to help protect individual privacy in LLMs by enabling evaluation of unlearning methods relevant to the Right to be Forgotten; the authors note that LLMs can breach individual privacy by regurgitating personal details or answering questions about people who would rather not have their information served through LLMs; effective unlearning methods are critical for safe and legally compliant AI deployment
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists entirely of fabricated, synthetic author profiles generated by GPT-4; no real personal or sensitive information is present, and the fictitious nature of the data ensures no remnants exist in model pretraining data
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating machine unlearning algorithms for large language models; studying the efficacy of unlearning methods in terms of forget quality and model utility; motivating development of better unlearning techniques relevant to the Right to be Forgotten
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was generated synthetically using GPT-4 prompted with predefined author attributes (birthplace, gender, birth year, genre, awards, parents' professions, and book title keywords seeded from the Goodreads Books dataset) to produce 20 question-answer pairs per fictitious author, ensuring diversity and minimizing bias from pretraining data. Paraphrased answers and five factually incorrect perturbations per question were generated using GPT-4 to support the Truth Ratio evaluation metric. The dataset was split into forget and retain sets at three severity levels (1%, 5%, and 10% forget proportions).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To reduce bias from GPT-4's pretraining data leaking into the synthetic author profiles, the authors used an elaborate prompt that deterministically seeds various author attributes (place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, parents' occupations, book title keywords). Book title keywords were randomly selected from the Goodreads Books dataset on Kaggle, drawing from two books per genre to ensure diversity. This replaced an initial generic prompt that produced biased outputs (e.g., overrepresentation of certain birth years, months, and recurring words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', 'whispers' in titles).
